records.text: Owens said Qatar stated that it had a relationship with Hamas because the U.S. government had asked it to establish one.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And they said, the reason why we have a relationship with Hamas is because the U.S. government asked us to establish one.

verification.notes: Qatar's Ministry of Foreign Affairs reports that the prime minister said Qatar's relationship with Hamas was established 13 years earlier at the request of the United States. An earlier CBS interview also records him saying the Hamas office was established in coordination with the United States to maintain communication. These primary and direct sources verify Owens's summary of what Qatar stated; they do not imply U.S. endorsement of Hamas's actions.

records.text: Candace Owens paraphrased Qatar as saying it worked with Hamas because Israel and the United States asked it to act as an intermediary, and that it was then attacked for doing what they requested.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Have they ever even done anything negative toward Israel? Well, Qatar recently came out and said, yeah, we work with Hamas because Israel and the United States asked us to. They asked us to play the intermediary. And now we are being attacked for doing what they asked us to do, which sounds like the most absolute United States Israel thing ever, is to ask people to help you and then to be like, I'm so horrified by what they're doing.

verification.notes: Transcript context at 4347.949 paraphrases a recent Qatari government response. Qatar's official news agency quotes the Foreign Ministry saying that hosting Hamas's political office occurred as part of mediation requested by both the United States and Israel and condemning Israel's attack on Qatari territory. The paraphrase accurately captures the core of that official position.

records.text: Future history books should not describe Gazans as the victims; they should identify Israel as the victim and Iran and Hamas as the aggressors.
records.speaker: Mike Pompeo

appearances.snippet: it's not that we don't forget. We need to make sure that the story is told properly so that when the history books write this, they don't write about the victims of Gaza, right? They can't. I should be a little more precise. There were victims in Gaza, right? It's true. There are civilian casualties in every war that's ever been fought. But the victims were the people of the nation state of Israel, though that the aggressor was the Iranian regime in the proxy of Hamas. And we need to make sure that the history books reflect that. And that requires each of us every day to talk about it in real time with our children, with our grandchildren, about it in a way that is serious and thoughtful and complete and moral.

verification.notes: Verified as an attributed opinion, not as an objective judgment about the conflict. In the primary clip played in the episode, Mike Pompeo said history books should not write about 'the victims of Gaza,' then clarified that civilian victims did exist in Gaza but argued that Israel was the victim and that Iran and Hamas were the aggressors. The source statement accurately captures the position he expressed, while his clarification is important context.

records.text: Hamas has no control in the West Bank, where 37 Palestinian children had been killed through August and 7,000 Palestinians had been killed since the occupation.
records.speaker: Bassem Youssef

appearances.snippet: Hamas has absolutely no control in the West Bank and this is the beginning of this street. ... Only through August, ... 37 Palestinian kids were killed. ... No music festival, ... no paragliding, ... no Hamas. Since the occupation of the West Bank, ... 7,000 Palestinians were killed.

verification.notes: The Palestinian Authority, not Hamas, administers parts of the West Bank, though Hamas maintains political and militant presence there. A contemporaneous child-rights report counted 37 Palestinian children killed across the occupied Palestinian territory by early August 2023, not solely the West Bank; the asserted 7,000-since-occupation total was not substantiated.

records.text: Benjamin Netanyahu funded Hamas.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I mean, who do you guys think funded Hamas? Benjamin Netanyahu did, obviously.

verification.notes: Netanyahu did not personally donate his own funds to Hamas, and he says transfers were intended for Gaza's civilian administration. However, reporting and Netanyahu's own interview confirm that governments under him approved and facilitated large Qatari transfers into Hamas-run Gaza; AP reports some money reached Hamas's military wing. Thus 'funded Hamas' captures material policy support but overstates the directness and purpose.
